newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - July 30th 1997.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - July 30th 1997.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- ON-SCREEN SHOPPING 'IN DEMAND'

A survey released by research firm Durlacher has indicated half of all UK Internet users would be interested in purchasing goods from the home, either via television or computer-based services. The survey was accompanied by statistics which show a shift in the 'typical Internet user' population from computer enthusiasts to highly-paid professionals.
-- GOLDEN VALE RETURNS TO THE BLACK

Irish dairy group Golden Vale has reported interim pre-tax profits for I6. 5m stg, compared with a loss of I47,000 stg in the previous period and helped by the popularity of processed cheese. Turnover for the first half was down four per cent to I278m stg due to lower volumes and costs for butter and milk products, although the cheese division recorded an profit of I2m stg compared with a loss of I300,000 stg in 1996.
-- STRONG POUND HURTS ISA AS CHIEF QUITS

ISA International, the toner cartridge to ink jet computer products group has released its first half results, which include a seven per cent increase in pre- tax profits to 4m stg and sales from continuing operations down 2.4 per cent to 119m stg. The group's figures were affected by of the strong pound, with a 360,000 stg interim profits hit and the resignation of its chief executive Peter Hildrew. ISA is currently in acquisition talks with various European companies.
THE TIMES
-- BT INVESTORS SEEK CLARIFICATION ON MERGER WITH MCI

Having seen over 5m stg taken from the value of their shares following MCI's profits warning earlier in the month, shareholders in British Telecom have demanded the company's board clarify the current state of the merger between the two groups. The merger has yet to be cleared by regulators in the US, with BT and MCI set to release their quarterly results before the end of the week.
-- TV FIRM BUYS ROYAL FILM

The Television Corporation has purchased 200 hours of footage of the Royal Family for an undisclosed amount of money, an acquisition expected to generate an additional 100,000 in sales at the group per year. The company has also made plans to open a Visual Arts studio which will contain computers which generate artificially moving images, rented out for a fee of 10,000 stg per day.
-- CIDER CHIEF'S 26 PER CENT RISE

It has been revealed that Richard Purdey, the chairman of cidermaker Merrydown, received 118,000 stg in pay for 1996, a 26 per cent rise which came despite pre-tax profits at the group down by over 50 per cent, at 821,000. Merrydown's managing director, Paul Milliman's salary was up 21.7 per cent to 98,000 stg. The company stated pay figures were set out at the beginning of the year, before sales of its products began to decrease.
THE GUARDIAN
-- RAIL FIRM IS FINED FOR AXING TRAINS

John O'Brien, the rail franchise director, has stated that from Monday he will levy a fine of 600 pounds sterling on Regional Railways North East for each train it cancels, and if no improvements are seen in the franchise's activities, the fines will become 'more excessive', including a possible revoke of the franchise's licence. The move follows a series of cancellations at Regional, which it blamed on a shortage of drivers.
-- NET FIRM FACES FRAUD INQUIRY

Peter Levin, the US chief executive of Internet software group Display IT, has admitted to having made a series of false statements to investors and his company is now the subject of an investigation by the Securities and Futures Authority and possibly the Department of Trade and Industry as well as the Serious Fraud Office. Display IT has announced the resignation of its auditors, Deloitte & Touche and confessed statements it made claiming a software licence purchase of 5.7m stg from a Luxembourg company were false.
-- WINDFALL THREAT TO PRICES

The deputy chairman of the Electricity Consumers' Commission, Ken Prior, has warned electricity customers they could face higher bills as a result of Labour's windfall profits tax. Prior stated the tax would lead to cuts in investment by electricity companies and urged the government to keep a close watch on the industry's activities in the run-up to its next price review.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- IT STAFF SHORTAGES WORSEN

IT services group Admiral has reported it is facing problems due to understaffing and soaring salaries in the computer industry, problems similar to those which earlier in the year led IT group Logica to issue a profits warning. Admiral has admitted to having awarded graduates 10 per cent salary increases, over twice as much as the average wage inflation due to the problem of a 20 per cent employee turnover count in the computer industry.
-- CABLE & WIRELESS FORCES CWC TO CURTAIL ITS SPENDING PLANS

Cable & Wireless Communications, the 4.5bn stg cable television and telephones offshoot of Cable & Wireless, is to reduce its investment plans as a result of its failure to meet profits targets set out by its parent company. It has also been revealed divisional directors were not consulted on the decision to award a multi-million CWC advertising campaign to London's Rapier Stead & Bowden. The spending reductions are expected to create further tensions between C&W chief executive Dick Brown and CW C's Graham Wallace.
-- SECOND DIRECTOR RESIGNS AT MFI

MFI furniture has announced the resignation of David Brock, the second director to resign from the company in July, as Trevor Tellett resigned earlier in the month. Brock's departure was reportedly due to the decrease of company activities in Germany, where most of Brock's responsibilities centred. The departure leaves MFI with four chief executive directors.
